title: Finite data and finite relations descend in a filtered colimit
statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ a directed system of commutative rings (ring maps $A_i\to A_j$ for $i\le j$, compatible) with colimit $A$ in the category of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Given
finitely many elements of $A$ and finitely many equalities between ring
expressions in those elements, there exists one stage $i$ and lifts of all
selected elements to $A_i$ for which all selected equalities hold. Once
they hold at $i$, they hold after every transition $A_i\to A_j$.

proof.text: A nonempty directed set, viewed as a category, is filtered, so [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] applies to the system $(A_i)$ of commutative rings. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] (1), choose a representative stage and lift for each selected element. Put these finitely many stages into a finite set and use directedness together with [lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound] to move all lifts to one common stage. Evaluate every selected ring expression on those lifts. Its image in the colimit is the corresponding selected element, so the asserted equality of two expressions is an equality of two representatives in the colimit. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] (2), each such equality holds after passing to some later stage. There are finitely many equalities; apply [lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound] to their witness stages and the common stage, and transport all equalities there. Ring homomorphisms preserve these equalities at every later stage.
